subject: Elmwood pilot: model qualification & quantization recommendations
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Eliza Wu <eliza@elmwood.ai>, Tom Horton <tom.horton@elmwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Elmwood pilot: model qualification & quantization recommendations

Hi team / Eliza + Tom — thanks again for a productive call. Quick recap and a recommended path for a short pilot that lets Elmwood validate latency and quality trade-offs without risking production regressions.

Call recap (what we heard)
- Use case: on-demand document summarization + semantic retrieval for enterprise docs (legal, contracts). Real-time expectation: sub-300ms tail for 256-token responses; peak ~150 rps, with bursts to 400 rps.
- Quality bar: human-rated summarization relevance >= 92% (baseline against current in-house model). Small hallucination tolerance; factuality is important.
- Data policy: documents are customer-owned, require strict audit logs and optional private deployment later.

Initial model candidates (recommended for pilot)
- OpenLlama-13B (FP16 baseline): good balance for semantic summarization, cheaper memory footprint.
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (FP16 baseline): strong instruction-following; useful for short-form summarization prompts.
- Llama-3-70B (sharded / quantized variants): target for quality headroom if throughput/infra allows.

Quantization trade-offs (summary) — we ran small-scale internal experiments and distilled the practical trade-offs:
- GPTQ (4-bit tuned): throughput ~1.8x over FP16 on A100s for 13B models; observed mean semantic-similarity delta ~-1.2% vs FP16 on our summarization promptset. Pros: reliable quality preservation for many instruction tasks; conservative.
- AWQ (4-bit mixed): throughput ~2.5x over FP16 on same HW for 13B; observed quality delta ~-2.8% on edge-case factuality prompts. Pros: better latency/cost; cons: occasional tail hallucinations on long-context retrieval.
- FP8 (fast path): throughput ~3.2x vs FP16 but with larger delta (~-3.5% on our measurements) and requires careful kernel support and monitoring. Good when latency is the strictest constraint and you can tolerate a small quality hit or run post-processing filters.

Operational knobs and mitigations
- Start pilot with GPTQ on 13B / Mistral to minimize regression risk. Run AWQ as a second arm for latency-sensitive routes only.
- Use prefix/KV caching for repeated long-context retrievals — that reduced token latency by ~18% in our tests.
- Add a quality guard: route a sample (1-5%) of requests to FP16 or Llama-3-70B to monitor drift; automatically fallback if semantic-sim drops below 90%.

Proposed pilot (48–72 hour A/B)
- Set up two serving arms on Redwood Dedicated: GPTQ(13B) and AWQ(13B). If capacity allows, add FP16 Llama-3-70B as a reference.
- Use the attached promptset (elmwood-promptset-v1.jsonl) + your internal dev-set for evaluation. We’ll instrument: latency p50/p95/p99, cost per 1k summaries, semantic similarity (embedding cosine against human refs), and hallucination rate (automated heuristics + small human sample).

Next steps & asks
1) Eliza/Tom: confirm you can share a ~200-sample labeled dev set (redacted) or give us permission to use the attached promptset + your QA team for a fast human check.
2) Monica/Karthik: I’ll need a Dedicated pool with 4x A100-equivalent capacity for 48h and preloaded models (GPTQ + AWQ builds).
3) Scheduling: propose a 30-minute tech-deep on Tuesday 5/21 to align infra + telemetry.

Attachments: elmwood-promptset-v1.jsonl (sample prompts), elmwood-benchmarks-template.csv, redwood-quant-trade-study-abridged.pdf

Thanks — I’ll stand up the GH notebook and baseline benchmarks as soon as Eliza confirms the sample set.

— Rishi

Eliza — great, thanks for the quick turnaround. Answers inline + short cost/ops notes.

On Tue, 17 May 2028 at 04:10:00 PM Eliza Wu <eliza@elmwood.ai> wrote:
> We can provide a 250-sample redacted dev set by Monday morning (PII removed).
That’s perfect — the dev set will let us compute a reliable semantic-similarity baseline and run human checks for hallucination.

> For the fallback sampling you suggested, what’s the expected additional cost overhead if we hold 1 A100-equivalent on FP16 as reference?
Estimate: adding a warm FP16 reference node (1 A100-equivalent) increases the pilot infra cost by ~18–24% depending on utilization because it raises baseline instance count. The incremental token cost is small (we’ll sample ~1–2% of requests), but instance-hour costs are the main driver. We’ll provide exact numbers in the cost sheet prior to spin-up.

> Can we run the pilot in our VPC (private deployment)?
Yes — we can run the pilot in Elmwood’s VPC under Redwood Private. Differences to note:
- Setup overhead: ~2 business days for network & KMS config (if you want HSM-backed keys add 1 day).
- Cost delta: Private deployments carry a platform fee + higher infra egress constraints; expect ~25–40% uplift vs hosted Dedicated for short pilots (we’ll include exact quote).

Recommended technical split for the pilot (actionable)
- Arm A: GPTQ-13B (primary for quality safe baseline).
- Arm B: AWQ-13B (latency-cost arm) — route 30% of traffic initially.
- Reference: FP16 Llama-3-70B (sampled 1–2% for drift detection).

Metrics & pass/fail (to be finalized in tech-deep)
- Latency: p95 < 300ms for 256-token responses on production-like burst profile.
- Quality: embedding cosine >= 0.92 vs human refs; hallucination rate < 6% on sampled checks.
- Cost: target < 0.65x current per-summary cost (your baseline).

I’ll attach a short cost estimate and a benchmark notebook link before the call. Monica/Karthik — can you provision the Dedicated/Private quote and a 48h node reservation for the proposed dates?

Thanks — see you Tuesday 10:30am PT.

— Rishi
